events.region: Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 NM out; Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 NM out
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to 20 nm west
of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 nm out...

* Until 100 AM EDT.

* At 1225 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 43 nm south of
Twenty-Eight Foot Shoal Light, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 PM MDT Friday the stage was 17.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 PM MDT Friday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.7 feet
late tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River will continue in and around
the communities of Conejos and Antonito due to excessive rainfall
over the previous couple days.

* WHERE...Southeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Conejos River, creeks, streams, and other
low-lying and flood-prone locations will continue overnight as high
water continues to flow downstream. Mandatory evacuations continue
along portions of the Conejos River near Antonito. The Conejos
River will continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier
rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1007 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
Antonito area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Stream gauges on the Conejos River and San Antonio River near
Manassa continue to show rising water.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Conejos, Bountiful and Ortiz.
- Highway 17 between Antonito and Cumbres Pass remains closed due
to flooding and debris.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central New Mexico, including Otero
County and portion of far west Texas including El Paso and Hudspeth
Counties.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of thunderstorms are expected to move through the
region between this evening and late Saturday night. Widespread
rainfall amounts of up to 1" are likely with localized areas
receiving 2-3" resulting in flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
